lines.trans: The main problem of men has always been very simple.
We do not know at all what women want.
Perhaps they simply like tormenting us for a long time.

words.gram: instrumental singular or dative plural pronoun

lines.trans: Oh, Denis, how heartless I really am!
Or they want to see us weak sometimes.
Then they can pity us and take care of us.
Daughter, it looks like your molecular show succeeded splendidly!
Denis, well what do you need from me again?
How many times must you repeat that there is nothing between us?
Take twenty thousand and hand her this fifty-ruble bill!
Just make sure you do not tell anyone about our deal!

examples.text: Отстань от меня, я не хочу разговаривать!
examples.trans: Leave me alone, I do not want to talk!

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'necessary'.

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить.
examples.trans: I need to make a call.

examples.text: Тебе нужно отдохнуть.
examples.trans: You need to rest.

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.
examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'how much'.

examples.text: Сколько раз повторять, между нами ничего нет?
examples.trans: How many times must you repeat that there is nothing between us?

examples.text: Сколько жвачки!
examples.trans: So much gum!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'time', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Я ещё раз спрашиваю, где мои загустители?

examples.text: Сколько раз повторять, между нами ничего нет?
examples.trans: How many times must you repeat that there is nothing between us?

examples.text: Один раз.
examples.trans: Just once.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (root 'вторять'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to repeat', forming an aspectual pair with 'повторить'.

examples.text: Сколько раз повторять, между нами ничего нет?
examples.trans: How many times must you repeat that there is nothing between us?

examples.text: Ещё раз повторяю, я решил вашу проблему.
examples.trans: I repeat once again, I solved your problem.

examples.text: Повторяйте за мной.
examples.trans: Repeat after me.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'between' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.text: Между прочим, я председатель суда.
examples.trans: For your information, I am the chairman of the court.

examples.text: Это останется между нами.
examples.trans: This will stay between us.

examples.text: Вы тут между собой договоритесь.
examples.trans: You two sort it out between yourselves here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('nothing') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.text: Тихо, ничего не говори, просто послушай меня!
examples.trans: Hush, do not say anything, just listen to me!

examples.text: Ничего, наша машина тебя сейчас быстро подвезёт!
examples.trans: No problem, our car will give you a quick ride right now!

examples.text: Сколько раз повторять, между нами ничего нет?
examples.trans: How many times must you repeat that there is nothing between us?

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('no') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя со мной нет никаких шансов.
examples.trans: You have no chances with me at all.

examples.text: Но у нас пока нет прямых доказательств.
examples.trans: But we do not have direct evidence yet.

examples.text: Сколько раз повторять, между нами ничего нет?
examples.trans: How many times must you repeat that there is nothing between us?

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to take', forming an aspectual pair with 'брать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Настя, возьми, пожалуйста, разменяй эти деньги.
examples.trans: Nastya, take this, please, and change this money.

examples.text: Возьми двадцать тысяч и передай ей этот полтинник!
examples.trans: Take twenty thousand and hand her this fifty-ruble bill!

examples.text: Возьмите на работу Галилея.
examples.trans: Go and hire Galileo.

meanings.note: Everyday conversational Russian num meaning 'twenty', frequent in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Возьми двадцать тысяч и передай ей этот полтинник!
examples.trans: Take twenty thousand and hand her this fifty-ruble bill!

examples.trans: I borrowed twenty thousand.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'thousand', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Возьми двадцать тысяч и передай ей этот полтинник!
examples.trans: Take twenty thousand and hand her this fifty-ruble bill!

examples.text: Это тысячи рабочих мест.
examples.trans: That means thousands of jobs.

examples.text: Тысяча рублей.
examples.trans: A thousand roubles.

передать.gloss: to pass on, to hand over

meanings.en: to pass on, to hand over
meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (root 'дать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to pass on', forming an aspectual pair with 'передавать'.

examples.text: Возьми двадцать тысяч и передай ей этот полтинник!
examples.trans: Take twenty thousand and hand her this fifty-ruble bill!

examples.text: Передай это Алексею.
examples.trans: Give this to Alexei.

examples.text: Передайте, пожалуйста, привет маме.
examples.trans: Please pass on my regards to your mum.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('she') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.text: Виктор Петрович, она же совсем молодая девушка!
examples.trans: Viktor Petrovich, she is a very young girl after all!

examples.text: Она приехала ко мне ненадолго в гости.
examples.trans: She came to visit me for a short while.

examples.text: Она из далёкого Владивостока на два дня прилетела!
examples.trans: She flew in from distant Vladivostok for two days!

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('this') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.text: Прекрати сейчас же всю эту нежную ерунду!
examples.trans: Stop all this mushy nonsense right now!

examples.text: Я очень прошу вас хранить эту тайну.
examples.trans: I earnestly ask you to keep this secret.

examples.text: Виктор Петрович, кто эта молодая девушка?
examples.trans: Viktor Petrovich, who is this young woman?

examples.text: Возьми двадцать тысяч и передай ей этот полтинник!
examples.trans: Take twenty thousand and hand her this fifty-ruble bill!

examples.text: Главная проблема мужчин всегда была очень простой.
examples.trans: The main problem of men has always been very simple.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'only'.

examples.text: Тут только мои личные вещи, а что?
examples.trans: There are only my personal things here, why?

examples.text: Могу сейчас сказать вам только одно.
examples.trans: I can tell you only one thing right now.

examples.text: Да, только Лёва просил пока молчать!
examples.trans: Yes, only Lyova asked to keep quiet for now!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (root 'мотреть'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to look', forming an aspectual pair with 'посмотреть'.

examples.text: Смотри, это билет на свидание со мной.
examples.trans: Look, this is a ticket for a date with me.

examples.text: Я смотрю, ты тут с Евой подружилась.
examples.trans: I see you have become friends with Eva here.

examples.text: Смотрите, он зашёл в этот дорогой ресторан.
examples.trans: Look, he went into this expensive restaurant.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('nobody') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.text: Никто не придаёт этому большого значения.
examples.trans: Nobody attaches great importance to this.

examples.text: Никто не войдёт.
examples.trans: Nobody will come in.

examples.text: Я знаю город как никто.
examples.trans: I know the town like nobody else.

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.en: to speak, to say, to talk
meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to speak', forming an aspectual pair with 'сказать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Но вчера вечером ты говорила совсем другое!
examples.trans: But last night you were saying something completely different!

examples.text: Вчера говорил напиток, а сейчас говорит начальник!
examples.trans: Yesterday the drink was speaking, and now the boss is speaking!

examples.text: Да, вы всегда так романтично говорите!
examples.trans: Yes, you always speak so romantically!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'about' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.text: Только смотри, никому не говори про наш уговор!
examples.trans: Just make sure you do not tell anyone about our deal!

examples.text: Он про меня гадости рассказывает.
examples.trans: He says nasty things about me.

examples.text: Она всё про всех знает.
examples.trans: She knows everything about everyone.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('our') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.text: Федя, вставай, наша новая начальница очень злая!
examples.trans: Fedya, get up, our new boss is very angry!

examples.text: До встречи в нашем любимом ресторане!
examples.trans: See you at our beloved restaurant!

examples.text: Случайность, а может быть, это наша судьба?
examples.trans: A fluke, or maybe it is our destiny?

examples.text: Только смотри, никому не говори про наш уговор!
examples.trans: Just make sure you do not tell anyone about our deal!

examples.text: Главная проблема мужчин всегда была очень простой.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to think', forming an aspectual pair with 'подумать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Я думаю, женщины просто хотят настоящей любви.

examples.text: Я думаю о работе.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'real', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Подождите, это что, настоящая жидкая курица?
examples.trans: Wait, is this real liquid chicken?

examples.text: Я думаю, женщины просто хотят настоящей любви.
examples.trans: I think women simply want real love.

examples.text: Это настоящий успех!
examples.trans: This is real success!

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'love', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Я думаю, женщины просто хотят настоящей любви.
examples.trans: I think women simply want real love.
